title: New Tesla Model Y v BYD Sealion: Ultimate review!
description:

It’s time for a showdown between two of the best mid-sized electric SUVs you can buy in 2025 - the Tesla Model Y vs the BYD Sealion! 

The question is, which will come out on top in this all-new group test? Let’s take a closer look at the two contenders. 

The new Model Y has been updated both inside & out compared to the previous model. On the outside, there’s a Cybertruck-inspired front light bar, new alloy wheel designs, and a redesigned rear bumper, coupled with an illuminated Tesla badge. On the inside, it’s still much of the same as in the old car, apart from a few minor tweaks and changes. Thankfully, there’s also still a stalk for the indicator, unlike in the new Model 3! 

In terms of price, the Model Y range starts from £44,990, rising to £52,000 for the top-of-the-range edition. The car we have here is the long-range edition, which has dual motors for AWD, 507hp, 494Nm, and a weight of 1,995kg. 

As for the BYD Sealion, it has a pretty imposing look from the outside, with large air intakes on either side of the front bumper. Around the back, there’s a small boot lip spoiler, as well as a full-length light bar. On the inside, there’s a number of differences to the Tesla. There’s leatherette throughout the cabin that gives it a smart feel, while there are a number of physical buttons and a drive mode select lever. There’s a large infotainment screen that can rotated, and the BYD also comes with a set of digital dials. 

The BYD starts from £47,000, rising to around £59,000 for the range-topping edition. We had the dual motor Excellence edition for this test, which delivers 530hp and 690Nm, and weighs in at 2,420kg. 

The long-term trip computers on these cars recorded energy consumption figures of 3.7 miles per kWh in the Tesla, and 2.5 miles per kWh in the BYD. The Tesla's 75kWh battery means it should manage around 278 miles on a full charge, while the BYD's 91.3kWh battery should deliver around 228 miles. 

So will the BYD come out on top? Or will the Tesla reign supreme? You’ll need to stick with Mat to see for yourself!

The Tesla Model Y has been updated! 

But this is no ordinary facelift - there are a whole load of changes both inside and out! Mat’s had a chance to get his hands on one before the official unveiling, and he’s about to run you through what’s changed. 

In terms of the design, there have been a whole load of updates. There’s a new bonnet and new wings on either side, and the headlights have been updated as well. A light bar has been added, too, which is giving serious Cybertruck vibes! Along the side, the only changes are new alloy designs, while around the back there’s an updated spoiler, new tail lights that reflect the light across the badge, and a new diffuser. All in all, the looks are a serious improvement over the original Y! 

On the inside the design is almost identical to the new Model 3. However, there’s one BIG change - the indicator stalk has returned in place of buttons on the steering wheel! Elsewhere, the changes are the same as in the Model 3. The seats are comfier and are now ventilated, and the dash design has been updated too. 

When it comes to performance, it comes with the same batteries and motors as the previous car. So this Launch Edition Model Y has dual motors to produce 384hp, as well as a 75kWh battery. There will be a single-motor edition, but the stats are yet to be revealed. 

The previous Model Y had a price tag of £52,000. In contrast, this new edition starts at £61,000 - a £9,000 increase! So is it worth it? You’ll need to stick with Mat to see for yourself!

title: Our honest opinion on the Model Y! //2026 Tesla Model Y review
description:
This is a couple car review of the 2026 Tesla Model Y compact, electric crossover vehicle. 
For the Canadian market, the 2026 Tesla Model Y is made in Berlin, Germany and for the US market, it’s made in the US. 
What’s New? The 2026 Tesla Model Y has improved handling, comfort, more responsive steering and a quieter ride. The exterior gets some tweaks, the front and rear lightbars have been redesigned to improve aerodynamics, range and efficiency. The interior has been updated with more soft touch finishes, acoustic glass, a larger 15.4” touchscreen, invisible speakers, ventilated front seats, a power recline second row and an 8” rear seat touchscreen has been added. 
We’re driving the 2026 Tesla Model Y Premium AWD model with 526 km, 327 miles of range. 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and it has a top speed of 201 km/h, 125 mph. Tesla doesn’t share horsepower and torque numbers. 
There is a 2026 Tesla Model Y Performance model with 492 km, 306 miles of range. 0-60 mph in 3.3 seconds and a top speed of 250 km/h, 155 mph. 
In the US, there are also two RWD models available, Standard with 321 miles of range and Premium 357 miles of range. 
The 2026 Tesla Model Y offers a lot of value with a starting price of $64,990 CAD for the Premium AWD model and $74,990 CAD for the Performance model. In the US, Standard RWD $39,990, Premium RWD $44,990, Premium AWD $48,990, Performance AWD $57,490.
The 2026 Tesla Model Y really shines when it comes to charging, you get up to 253 km/157 miles of range in 15 minutes at a Tesla Supercharger. The Performance model at little less at 229 km/142  miles.
We are so impressed with the full-self driving feature which our model has for $11,000 CAD/$8,000 USD. Whether you are in the city or on the highway, the vehicle drives itself. You just sit back and enjoy the view. 
Thank you so much to Charlie Wang, the General Manager at the Tesla Port Coquitlam dealership. We appreciate you lending us this Model Y to review.

title: Tesla Car CRIES in Indian Traffic: Autopilot Says ‘No Thanks’ #shorts
description:
Tesla officially entered the Indian market in July 2025 by launching its first showroom in Mumbai’s Bandra Kurla Complex. The company introduced the Model Y, offering two variants: Standard and Long-Range Rear-Wheel Drive. The prices are set around ₹60 lakh and ₹68 lakh, making it a premium option in India’s growing electric vehicle segment. Alongside the car launch, Tesla also unveiled its first Supercharger stations in Mumbai and Delhi, signaling its commitment to supporting EV infrastructure in the country.

However, Tesla’s much-talked-about Autopilot feature is struggling to adjust to Indian roads. While the system works well on highways in structured environments, Indian traffic presents a very different challenge. The Autopilot relies on clear lane markings, predictable traffic flow, and disciplined driving—features that are often missing in many Indian cities.

Roads filled with varied vehicle types, unexpected turns, poor signage, and irregular lane use confuse the system. The presence of stray animals, potholes, and unmarked diversions only adds to the complexity. As a result, Autopilot disengages often, requiring constant driver attention and intervention.

At this stage, Tesla's Autopilot in India serves more as an advanced driver-assist system than a true step toward autonomous driving. Until the software is further localized and Indian infrastructure sees improvement, full self-driving remains more of a long-term goal than a current reality.

title: Tesla Model Y: Honest Review After 15k Miles - The Good AND The Bad
description:
The Refresh Juniper Model Y has been delivering to customers now for about 10 months and we were able to get our Launch Series LR AWD Model Y in the first month or two of deliveries. Since then, we have put on over 15k miles over about 9 months and have truly had a chance to give the car a full shakedown. 

There is a lot to like about the new Tesla Model Y, and that really shouldn't be a surprise given the success of the previous generation. This new refreshed Model Y takes the previous gen car and steps up the comfort in a big way. Between the sound proofing and the ride comfort, the New Model Y feels like a completely different car on the road with a much more comfortable and refined ride. 

That isn't to say there aren't some drawbacks to this updated version of the Tesla Model Y. First thing that comes to mind is the fact that there is no longer a traditional gear shift knob, like we saw in the refresh Model 3, Model S, Model X and Cybertruck. Unlike those other variants though, the Model Y did keep the turn signal stalk, which was a smart move when trying to attract the average consumer. 

The updated features on this car include some heavy hitters like cooled front seats, a rear screen, updated front and rear ends. The lighting as a whole, inside and out, improve the overall experience in the car for both drivers and passengers. 

Of course Hardware 4 has been out for some time in the Model Y now, and that is still the case for now. HW5 is rumored to be around the corner and will likely be fitted to the upcoming models shortly after launch. This doesn't guarantee that the HW4 vehicles wont be as capable, but the new HW5 specs seem to be rather impressive, which would likely lead to a much more capable system for autonomous driving. 

Speaking of FSD, the experience has been relatively great in our Model Y, although it would be impossible to forget our unfortunate mishap during a coast to coast attempt on V13 FSD. After colliding with an object in the road, the vehicle started to slowly lose its ability to charge. Fortunately we were able to make it to a Service Center before it completely stopped working.

It turned out the HV battery pack was already on its way to an irreversible cell imbalance. The HV battery pack failed at about 15k miles, which is very uncommon for Tesla, and certainly the first time I have experienced a pack failure. 

Other than these things, the refresh Model Y is such a great car. It's a value unmatched by other options on the market. It comes with price, comfort, space, and tech. It truly is the full package and will continue to outsell most other cars on the market for the foreseeable future.

title: The Cheapest Model Y Is The Only Tesla You Need | Full Review
description:
Voices on the internet say the Tesla Model Y Standard is a variant to avoid. They argue that all the equipment it loses in the quest for improved affordability is enough to make it not worth considering. But is that really true?

Most of the criticism boils down to one idea: Tesla cut comfort and convenience features and that all adds up to make it feel cheap. So I treated the Standard like a normal car for almost two weeks, waiting for the moment it started to feel compromised and like a bad choice. It never came.

Sure, it’s not as nice as the Model Y Premium, whose suite of features does make it feel a cut above, but the Standard is still a lot of electric crossover for the money. Here in Romania, where I tested it, its €39,990 price tag before any incentives or discounts are applied makes it a very attractive buy. 

(Note: In the U.S., Tesla no longer calls this the “Standard,” instead labeling it the Model Y, with the more typical version now called the Model Y Premium. For clarity, we refer to it as the Standard throughout.)

You can’t get another similar EV here for less, and even in Standard trim, the Model Y has more standard equipment than more expensive rivals like the very popular Skoda Enyaq, which you see a lot around here (starting at just under €43,000).

What €39,990 buys you is the same body, the same packaging, and the same core usability as the regular Model Y, including access to the vast network of Superchargers, a genuinely massive cargo area and more performance than other base models.

The only other electric crossover that starts around the same price point in Europe is the Ford Explorer EV (based on Volkswagen’s MEB platform), but it’s a foot shorter, smaller inside, and not particularly premium-feeling. Probably the best alternative here in Europe is a base Hyundai Ioniq 5, which has a larger battery and more range. It only costs from €41,000, delivering 354 miles (570 km) WLTP on one charge, while the Tesla can only reach 331 miles (534 km), albeit with a smaller battery pack.

It’s a slightly different story in the U.S., where you can get rivals for less than its $39,990 starting price. The Chevrolet Equinox EV, Toyota bZ and Ford Mustang Mach-E in base trim all undercut the Model Y Standard and offer comparable specs. The Standard, therefore, makes more sense in Europe than in the States, where more affordable options are available.

But even if it’s not as cheap as rivals and in the U.S., does that mean you should avoid the Model Y Standard?

title: Saving Tesla dash cam footage without honking the horn!
description:
The Tesla dash cam feature is saving all the footage from the cameras around the car to the USB stick in the glovebox. But this is being constantly overwritten unless you specifically tell the car to keep the footage. The default method is to honk the horn and then the last 10 minutes of footage is saved and not overwritten. However, there are some instances where honking the horn would be confrontational or less than ideal. What you can do is drop the dashcam icon down to the shortcut bar, then while driving, a quick tap on that icon does the same and is far better than honking the horn.
Or you can use the voice control and say "save dash cam" or you can setup the left scroll wheel hold to be a shortcut to save the dash cam.
To learn more about Tesla's dash cam and Sentry mode, see the full video https://youtu.be/nwW2TEpiTTs
The vehicle is a 2024 Tesla Model Y RWD (HW3) with the 62.5kWh (60,5 kWh usable) LFP battery and when filming this was on software version 2025.26.4.

title: Tesla Model Y RWD LFP battery degradation after 18,000 miles and 1.5 years
description:
My Tesla Model Y rear wheel drive has the 60kWh LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate) battery pack which uses prismatic cells from CATL. The usable capacity is around 57-58 kWh. Tesla recommends that the LFP battery is charged to 100% at least once a week  to maintain an accurate state of charge and range calculation.
My car is now 15 months old and has done 18,000 miles and because I get free Supercharging, it has almost exclusively been DC rapid charged to 100% since new. Yet it has only lost 1 mile of range (using Tesla's EPA range estimate) over this period. That's only 0.38% degradation!
Many worry about battery life in EVs. In all new electric cars, the battery is warranted for 8 years. But the reality is that in most cases, the battery will outlast the rest of the vehicle.
This video was filmed in May 2025.

title: New 2026 Tesla Model Y L Review | Tesla's Luxury 6-Seater SUV Is Here!
description:
Tesla Model Y L Review 2026 | Tesla's Luxury 6-Seater SUV Is Here!
Today, we’re Reviewing the Tesla Model Y L 2026, Tesla's Luxury 6-Seater SUV which everyone’s been talking about. The brand-new 2026 Tesla Model YL is built on the success of the Model Y, the Model YL isn’t just a stretched version, it’s a fully reimagined, family-focused SUV with premium upgrades across design, space, and performance. We’ll explore how the Model Y L takes everything people love about the Model Y and elevates it into a true luxury six-seater experience. From styling to tech, cargo to comfort, this is the ultimate Model Y evolution. Let’s dive in!

Exterior Evolution – Front Fascia & Design

- The Model YL showcases a refreshed front design, mirroring the premium aesthetics seen on the Juniper Model Y refresh, such as a sleeker, more streamlined nose and a minimalistic bumper. 
- The new star gold paint option adds a high-end flair that instantly elevates perceived exclusivity.
- A standout new feature: a single daytime running light bar spans the front, offering both style and distinctive identity.
- For practical visibility, Tesla has added a front bumper camera with an ultra-wide view and a self-cleaning nozzle—a smart solution for harsh weather.

Stretching the Silhouette – Side Profile

- The “L” in Y L stands for “long”: the wheelbase stretches 150 mm (≈6 in) longer, and overall length increases by 179 mm (≈7 in).
- This extension isn’t just about space—it gives the Y L a more grounded, elegant presence and completely alters its side profile.
- The 19-inch Mecha Wheels feature an aerodynamic star-pattern that helps preserve range despite added mass.

Rear Design & Aerodynamics 

- At the back, the Model Y L embraces the modern full-width taillight aesthetic seen across Tesla's latest models. 
- The revamped C-pillar and a more pronounced ducktail spoiler enhance high-speed stability using form-follows-function design.
- Updated Model YYY badging subtly nods to its three-row, six-seat layout with a clever twist.

Space & Cargo – The Family Advantage 

- The six-seat (“2+2+2”) layout shines. Even with all seats upright, there's space for multiple grocery bags—but fold the second and third rows, and cargo swells to a massive 2,539 liters (≈89.7 cu ft). 
- The YL maintains the front frunk for small essentials—a practical bonus for family trips.

Interior Luxury – Comfort for All Rows 

- Third Row: Heated seats, air vents on C-pillars, simplistic manual door handles, and fold buttons—cozy for kids or short adult trips, though headroom and thigh support remain constrained. 
- Second Row: Premium captain’s chairs with heating, ventilation, powered armrests, and an electric slide feature—offering first-class experience.
- A central 8-inch screen empowers second-row occupants to control climate, entertainment, and even the front passenger seat.
- Overhead, the seamless acoustic glass roof bathes the cabin in light while keeping noise minimal.

Front Row & Tech – Driver & Passenger Enhancements

- Front seats are sculpted for long-haul comfort—featuring adjustable headrests and thigh extensions, plus heating and ventilation.
- The minimalist dashboard is accented with aluminum trims, ambient lighting, and a premium black headliner.
- Tesla retains the classic indicator stalk, a win for intuitive control in roundabouts. 
- The center console features dual wireless pads (50 W driver-side, 30 W passenger-side) with active cooling—ideal for fast-charging smartphones.
- Dominating control is the 16-inch touchscreen—slightly larger than the standard Model Y's 15.4-inch display, sharper, and supremely responsive.

Performance & Range Metrics 

- Under the hood lurks a dual-motor AWD system, producing about 340 kW (~456 hp). 
- You’ll nail 0–100 km/h in 4.5 seconds and achieve 201 km/h (≈125 mph) top speed.
- The 82 kWh NMC battery delivers a 751 km CLTC range (~466 mi). 
Wikipedia
- Quick-charging capability keeps it practical for long drives—Tesla claims strong range recovery during fast charging sessions.

Pricing & Market Strategy 

- Launching in China, the Model Y L starts at 339,000 RMB (~$47,000 USD)—about 8% more than a standard Model Y. 
- Deliveries begin September 2025, with strong demand already reported.
- Elon Musk hinted the Y L might not reach U.S. markets, depending on autonomous-driving rollout. 
- The move counters local Chinese competitors like Li Auto and Xiaomi as Tesla reignites its presence in a shrinking market.

title: Tesla Model S Plaid: New Info from Chief Designer and Engineer | Jay Leno's Garage
description:
Jay Leno sits down with the masterminds behind the latest Tesla Model S: Chief Designer Franz von Holzhausen and Lead Engineer Lars Moravy. This episode offers an exclusive look into the new updates and design philosophies that make the latest Model S the "best version of this car" ever built.

Unveiling New Technology:

Carbon Ceramic Brakes: The duo details the new carbon ceramic brakes, now a standard option on the Plaid. Unlike other carbon brakes, these are made with a continuous carbon matrix, providing excellent stopping power even when cold. This is especially useful for one-pedal driving, which Jay says has left his own car's original brake pads in near-perfect condition.

Thermal System & Range: Discover the new "super minimal version two" thermal system, which uses a cast aluminum manifold to improve cooling and heating efficiency for the entire powertrain. This has increased the real-world range on the long-range model to 410 miles and significantly narrowed the gap between sticker and real-world range.

Aerodynamic Improvements: Learn how Tesla uses aerodynamic design with new wheels and optional caps to improve efficiency and range.

Design & Performance Insights:

Power and Speed: The Model S Plaid boasts 1020 horsepower, a 0-60 mph time under 2 seconds, a 200 mph top speed, and a quarter-mile time of 9.20 seconds.

Manufacturing Quality: Franz and Lars reveal how years of refinement have led to tighter panel gaps and better overall build quality. They also explain the benefits of Tesla's water-based paint, which makes it easier to color-match for repairs.

The Yoke Steering Wheel: The team discusses the yoke steering wheel and why its design allows drivers to see the entire dashboard without obstruction.

Interior Upgrades: Explore the upgraded interior, including new ambient lighting that can sync with music, and a larger rear screen with a unique dual-audio feature for passengers using Bluetooth headphones.

Join Jay, Franz, and Lars as they take this incredible car for a test drive and share firsthand details about its groundbreaking features.

title: Mercedes FINALLY beats the Tesla Model 3? Mercedes CLA EQ 250+ first drive review
description:
It's taken a while, but Mercedes might have finally knocked the Tesla Model 3 off its perch.

The new electric CLA – or Mercedes CLA 250+ with EQ Technology to be exact – has a staggering 484 mile range with a fully charged battery.

It's also built with 800 volt architecture, much like the Porsche Taycan and Hyundai Ioniq 5, meaning it can rapid charge at some super quick 320kW speeds.

Mercedes has also filled it to the brim with technology, including an AI-enhanced new operating system that lets you talk to the car like it's a human being.

But is all this enough to beat the likes of the Tesla Model 3, BYD Seal, Polestar 2 and so on? We've been in Copenhagen to find out.

title: Я не понял, почему Tesla меня зацепила
description:
тест драйв Tesla опыт, первый раз за рулем Tesla, Tesla стоит ли покупать, ощущения от Tesla, Tesla плюсы и минусы, электромобиль Испания, Tesla отзыв владельца

Я решил проверить, почему все так хвалят Tesla, и записался на тест-драйв. Без ожиданий — просто из любопытства.

Честно, я не планировал покупать Tesla. Сначала рассматривал более привычные варианты: гибриды, Audi e-tron, машины, которые понятны и предсказуемы. Но вокруг меня всё больше людей пересаживаются на Tesla, и я не видел ни одного откровенно недовольного владельца.

В этом видео делюсь первым опытом: как проходит тест-драйв Tesla и какие ощущения возникают с первых минут.

Интересный момент — тебе дают не максимальную комплектацию, а самую обычную версию. Без “вау-эффектов”, без премиальных опций. И именно это делает опыт честным: ты сразу понимаешь, что из себя представляет машина без маркетинга.

Но даже в такой версии произошло то, чего я не ожидал.

Я не могу это объяснить рационально. Это не про цифры, не про характеристики и не про “лучше/хуже”. Это какое-то ощущение, что машина тебя зацепила.

До этого я ездил на разных автомобилях: Audi, Mercedes, Volkswagen — и у всех есть свой характер. Но здесь ощущение другое.

И самое интересное — в тот момент я не понимал, почему.

Только позже, когда начал разбираться глубже, пришло понимание, что именно создаёт этот эффект.

В этом видео рассказываю:
— как проходит тест-драйв Tesla
— чем отличается первое ощущение от других машин
— почему Tesla цепляет даже в базовой версии

Но после этого я решил подойти к вопросу рационально — как инвестор.

И там всплыла одна деталь, которая сильно повлияла на решение.

В следующей серии расскажу, что именно это было.

Подписывайтесь, если интересны реальные кейсы, деньги и выборы, которые мы делаем в жизни.

title: Tesla vs Audi e tron. Мой Неожиданный Тест Драйв!
description:
Tesla стоит ли покупать, Tesla или Audi e tron сравнение, электромобиль Испания выбор, тест драйв Tesla опыт, стоит ли переходить на электромобиль, Tesla плюсы и минусы

Я долго не понимал, почему все так хвалят Tesla. Каждый второй говорит, что это лучший опыт вождения, но у меня были сомнения.

Когда встал вопрос, на что пересесть после дизеля, я изначально смотрел в сторону более привычных решений. Рассматривал гибриды из-за налоговых преимуществ, думал про Audi e-tron, так как уже ездил на Audi и понимал, чего ожидать от машины.

Но в какой-то момент я поймал себя на мысли: если уж переходить на электричку, может стоит попробовать Tesla? Тем более, вокруг меня всё больше людей ездят на Tesla, и я не видел ни одного откровенно недовольного владельца.

В этом видео рассказываю:
— как я выбирал между гибридом, Audi и Tesla
— какие сомнения были перед переходом на электромобиль
— почему Tesla сначала не входила в мой список
— как я в итоге решил записаться на тест-драйв

Основные страхи были стандартные: зарядка, удобство, дальние поездки, привязка к инфраструктуре. Всё это кажется неудобным, если раньше ездил только на ДВС.

Но интерес взял верх, и мы решили проверить это на практике.

И именно на тест-драйве произошло то, чего я совсем не ожидал.

Это не обзор и не реклама, а личный путь выбора и размышлений, с которыми сталкивается почти каждый перед покупкой электромобиля.

В следующей серии расскажу, что меня реально удивило, когда я впервые сел за руль Tesla.

Подписывайтесь, если интересны темы денег, переезда и реальных решений из жизни.

title: 2016 Nissan Leaf EV owner says cost of battery replacement may not be worth investment
description:
Neil Turner says he considers himself an environmentalist and an advocate for electric vehicles. Back in 2019, the B.C. resident says he purchased a used 2016 Nissan Leaf electric vehicle.

"The cost was $17,000 CDN including tax,” Turner told Consumer Matters.

Turner says his EV was driving well until this past winter during a cold snap. He says the battery range began to drop a kilometre a second, forcing him to take the car to his local Nissan dealership, where he was told the battery needed replacing.

“We went back and asked, can we have a quote for a replacement battery and that’s when I got the shock,” said Turner.

Turner was quoted over $85,846.55 CDN for the replacement battery. The quote did not include labour costs. “I almost fell down,” Turner said.

Consumer Matters reporter Anne Drewa explains what happened next.

title: Here's my RANGE and efficiency results on the 2026 Nissan LEAF. Skip Tesla?
description:
#nissanleaf #ev #tesla #rangetest 

I test the new 2026 Nissan Leaf's city and highway range. Here's the pros and the cons.

The all-new 2026 Nissan LEAF offers a sleek and streamlined design, an effortless charging experience, improved battery range1, and even greater value for money. The 2026 Nissan LEAF will reach Nissan dealerships this fall with Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Prices (MSRP) for the S+ grade starting at $29,9902 – the lowest starting MSRP for any new EV currently on sale in the U.S.3

Nissan's commitment to making EV mobility accessible to all is demonstrated by the new LEAF's MSRP being lower than it was 15 years ago, when the 2011 LEAF carried a list price of $32,780.

Additionally, the 2026 SV+ grade has an MSRP of $34,230, undercutting the 2025 LEAF SV PLUS by $1,960 despite offering dramatically more standard features and an increased driving range.

"The LEAF really kicked off the mainstream EV market when it launched 15 years ago, and Nissan's still committed to making electric driving accessible to all," said Vinay Shahani, senior vice president of U.S. Marketing and Sales at Nissan. "We've stuck to our mission of engineering EVs that are affordable but packed with value. That's how we've kept the LEAF's price steady over three generations — all while giving owners more style, more technology, more features and a vastly improved driving range over the original 2011 model."

The all-new LEAF features a longer driving range of up to 303 miles per charge1, and built-in North American Charging Standard (NACS) compatibility with Plug & Charge4 provides seamless access to more than 20,000 Tesla Superchargers for convenient public charging5, making LEAF ideal for commuting and road trips alike.

LEAF's modern design includes clean, minimalist surfacing and details like motorized flush door handles, a Nissan-first for a production car; a sleek, curving roofline, featuring a katana blade element inspired by the Z sports car; and a segment-first dimming panoramic roof6, which can transition between opaque and transparent at the touch of a button. The airy, spacious cabin features dual displays (12.3 inches, S/S+; 14.3 inches, SV+/PLATINUM+); an open, flat floor beneath the dashboard; and redesigned seats that enhance second-row knee room.

Advanced technology throughout makes living with LEAF effortless and enjoyable. Available Google built-in7, including Google Maps, streamlines navigation with Intelligent Route Planner, and the use of other familiar apps. New-to-LEAF camera tech includes standard, class-exclusive Intelligent Around View® Monitor8, standard Invisible Hood View8 and standard Front Wide View8 functions.

Having rather lost its way with electric cars, Nissan is now back with a third generation LEAF model that aims to return to the sharp end of the family hatch EV class. There's everything you might expect from a LEAF - but also perhaps, a lot that you wouldn't.

When the history books on the origins of electric cars are written, one early model will be prominent: the Nissan LEAF. First launched back in 2010 and followed up by second generation version in 2018, it's been described as the 'godfather' of electric cars - the very first volume-selling mainstream family EV. title: 2026 Nissan LEAF First Drive Review
description:
Fifteen years after it kickstarted the affordable EV movement, the Nissan Leaf is back — smarter, smoother, and more refined than ever. In this first drive review, Matt takes the all-new 2026 Nissan Leaf through Prince Edward County’s scenic roads to find out if the pioneer of mainstream electrification still deserves its reputation as the “Prius of EVs.”

The third-generation Leaf trades its familiar hatchback shape for a sleeker, more 4-door-coupe-like crossover design — but don’t worry, it hasn’t forgotten what made it great. It’s still practical, efficient, and priced for real people, not just early adopters.

Powered by a 214-hp electric motor and a 75-kWh liquid-cooled battery, the new Leaf delivers up to 488 km of range on a single charge, with 150 kW DC fast charging that goes from 10 to 80% in about 35 minutes. The ride is impressively quiet and composed, thanks to a reworked chassis and multi-link rear suspension. Inside, drivers are greeted by available twin 14.3-inch displays, recycled fabric materials, and excellent visibility — a cabin that feels modern yet refreshingly down to earth.

But what really stands out is how *effortless* it all feels. The 2026 Leaf has quietly perfected the art of daily driving. Whether it’s commuting, weekend getaways, or surviving another Canadian winter, this is an EV built for real life.

2026 Nissan Leaf Highlights:
• 214 hp / 261 lb-ft of torque for smooth, quiet acceleration
• Up to 488 km of NRCan range with the 75-kWh battery
• 150 kW DC fast charging (10–80% in ~35 minutes)
• Available Plug & Charge capability via the Nissan Energy Charge Network
• Comfortable, minimalist interior with available twin 14.3-inch displays

title: Premier essai Nissan LEAF 2026
description:
Quinze ans après avoir lancé le mouvement des véhicules électriques abordables, la Nissan Leaf est de retour — plus intelligente, plus fluide et plus raffinée que jamais. Dans cet essai routier, Matt met à l’épreuve la toute nouvelle Nissan Leaf 2026 sur les routes pittoresques du comté de Prince Edward afin de déterminer si la pionnière de l’électrification grand public mérite toujours sa réputation de « Prius des véhicules électriques ».

La troisième génération de la Leaf troque sa silhouette familière de hayon pour un design de multisegment plus élancé, rappelant un coupé à quatre portes — mais pas d’inquiétude, elle n’a rien perdu de ce qui faisait sa force. Elle demeure pratique, efficace et offerte à un prix accessible pour de vraies personnes, pas seulement pour les premiers adeptes de la mobilité électrique.

Propulsée par un moteur électrique de 214 chevaux et une batterie refroidie par liquide de 75 kWh, la nouvelle Leaf offre jusqu’à 488 km d’autonomie sur une seule charge, avec une capacité de recharge rapide en courant continu de 150 kW permettant de passer de 10 à 80 % en environ 35 minutes. La conduite est remarquablement silencieuse et équilibrée, grâce à un châssis retravaillé et à une suspension arrière multibras. À bord, les conducteurs sont accueillis par deux écrans de 14,3 pouces disponibles, des matériaux de tissu recyclé et une excellente visibilité — un habitacle à la fois moderne et agréablement terre à terre.

Mais ce qui impressionne vraiment, c’est à quel point tout semble *sans effort*. La Leaf 2026 a discrètement perfectionné l’art de la conduite quotidienne. Qu’il s’agisse des trajets quotidiens, des escapades de fin de semaine ou de la survie à un autre hiver canadien, cette voiture électrique est conçue pour la vraie vie.

Faits saillants de la Nissan Leaf 2026 :
• 214 ch / 261 lb-pi de couple pour une accélération douce et silencieuse
• Jusqu’à 488 km d’autonomie (données RNCan) avec la batterie de 75 kWh
• Recharge rapide en courant continu de 150 kW (de 10 à 80 % en environ 35 minutes)
• Fonction Plug & Charge offerte via le réseau Nissan Energy Charge
• Intérieur confortable et minimaliste avec double écran de 14,3 pouces disponible
• Prix de départ sous la barre des 45 000 $, avant frais

title: 2026 Nissan Leaf – review – back on top? | What Car?
description:
The Nissan Leaf has always been a pioneer — one of the first mainstream electric vehicles that made EV ownership accessible to the masses. Now, for 2026, Nissan has completely reimagined the Leaf to meet the demands of a new generation of electric mobility. The result? A bold, efficient, and high-tech EV that feels more premium and capable than ever.

Exterior: Futuristic and Aerodynamic

The 2026 Nissan Leaf departs dramatically from its familiar hatchback shape and embraces a sleek, fastback-inspired crossover design. Its smooth, sculpted body lines are not just for show — they enhance aerodynamics for improved range and performance.

At the front, the closed grille integrates seamlessly with the LED headlights, creating a sharp, modern face. The new light signature stretches across the hood line, emphasizing width and sophistication. From the side, flush door handles and a gently sloping roofline deliver a dynamic silhouette, while the floating roof design adds a futuristic touch.

Available 19-inch aero wheels and a palette of two-tone finishes complete the sporty and elegant exterior.

Interior: Minimalist Luxury Meets Smart Technology

Inside, the 2026 Leaf feels like a major step forward. The cabin combines minimalist design with premium materials such as soft-touch vegan leather, recycled textiles, and ambient LED lighting.

A large 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster and a 13-inch infotainment touchscreen dominate the dashboard, powered by the latest NissanConnect system with Google built-in and wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto support.

The center console is now more open and practical, offering additional storage space and a wireless charging pad. Rear passengers benefit from increased legroom, while the flat floor architecture makes the interior feel airy and spacious.

Performance: Stronger, Smarter, and More Efficient

The 2026 Leaf is built on Nissan’s latest EV platform, which also underpins the Ariya. Buyers can choose between two battery options — a 60 kWh pack for standard range and an 87 kWh pack for long-range models.

The long-range version delivers up to 440 miles (≈708 km) on a single charge under the WLTP cycle, making it one of the most efficient EVs in its class. With dual-motor all-wheel drive available, the 2026 Leaf produces up to 320 horsepower and 600 Nm of torque, ensuring quick acceleration and confident handling.

Regenerative braking and Nissan’s signature e-Pedal 2.0 enhance energy recovery and driving ease, while the updated thermal management system ensures consistent performance in all climates.

Charging and Connectivity

The new Leaf supports 350 kW DC fast charging, allowing the battery to go from 10% to 80% in just about 20 minutes. Home charging is easier too, thanks to an upgraded 22 kW AC onboard charger.

Remote access through the NissanConnect app lets users check battery status, schedule charging, and precondition the cabin before driving. Over-the-air software updates ensure the car’s systems stay up to date.

Safety and Driver Assistance

The 2026 Nissan Leaf comes standard with ProPILOT Assist 3.0, offering semi-autonomous highway driving with automated lane changes and adaptive cruise control. A 360° camera system, blind-spot warning, emergency braking with pedestrian detection, and driver attention monitoring all come standard.

Its structural rigidity and advanced driver-assist systems make the new Leaf one of the safest EVs Nissan has ever built.

Pricing and Availability

Expected to launch globally in mid-2026, the new Leaf will start around $39,000 USD for the base model and reach up to $55,000 for the high-performance AWD variant. Nissan aims to position it as a practical yet premium alternative to rivals like the Tesla Model 3, Hyundai Ioniq 6, and Volkswagen ID.7.

Verdict: A Reinvented Legend

The 2026 Nissan Leaf isn’t just an upgrade — it’s a rebirth. With its sophisticated design, long range, cutting-edge tech, and strong performance, it’s ready to compete in a rapidly evolving EV landscape.

The original Leaf made electric driving mainstream. The 2026 model proves that Nissan is ready to make it exciting again.

title: 2026 Nissan Leaf — Japan’s Silent Electric Blade Cutting Through the Future
description:
The 2026 Nissan Leaf does not roar into the future—it glides there, like a neon-lit whisper cutting through the noise of gasoline nostalgia. While others shout with brute force, this Japanese pioneer chooses precision, calm confidence, and an almost poetic restraint. The Leaf has always been a symbol, but in 2026, it becomes a statement.
Visually, the exterior feels sharper, cleaner, and more intentional. The body lines flow like wind-shaped metal, with aerodynamic sculpting that seems carved by electricity itself. Slim LED headlights stare forward with quiet intelligence, while the closed-off grille reminds you this car breathes differently. Subtle blue accents and futuristic wheel designs reinforce its identity as a machine born from Japan’s obsession with efficiency and harmony.
Inside, the Leaf transforms into a digital sanctuary. The dashboard is dominated by a wide, high-resolution display that merges infotainment and driver data into one fluid visual experience. Touch-sensitive controls, minimalist layouts, and eco-conscious materials create an interior that feels both modern and ethical. Nissan’s latest driver-assistance suite works silently in the background, reducing stress and elevating confidence without stealing attention.
Under the skin, the 2026 Nissan Leaf delivers refined electric performance. With improved battery density and smarter energy management, range anxiety fades into irrelevance for daily life. Acceleration from 0–100 km/h in approximately 7.5 seconds isn’t about thrill-seeking—it’s about instant, seamless motion. The torque arrives like a thought becoming action, immediate and smooth.
In the competitive EV landscape, the Leaf stands toe-to-toe with rivals like the Chevrolet Bolt EV, Hyundai Kona Electric, and Volkswagen ID.3. While some competitors chase aggressive styling or raw numbers, the Leaf positions itself as the intelligent all-rounder—balanced, dependable, and accessible.
Pricing remains one of its strongest weapons. The 2026 Nissan Leaf continues to offer exceptional value, undercutting many rivals while delivering proven technology. Long-term ownership is where it truly shines: low maintenance costs, reduced insurance premiums in many markets, and slower depreciation compared to early-generation EVs make it a rational yet emotionally satisfying choice.
On the road, the driving experience is serene and surprisingly engaging. The low center of gravity keeps corners composed, while regenerative braking turns everyday driving into an interactive energy dance. It’s not a sports car—and it doesn’t pretend to be. Its weakness lies in limited high-performance appeal, but its strength is clarity of purpose.
The 2026 Nissan Leaf is not trying to impress everyone. It’s speaking directly to those who understand that the future doesn’t always arrive loudly—it arrives inevitably.
Step into Japan’s electric vision. Drive the silence. Choose the future—now.

title: Este é o novo Nissan LEAF. Pai dos elétricos está IRRECONHECÍVEL
description:
A Nissan acaba de revelar a nova geração do LEAF, que passou pela maior transformação da sua história. E podemos mesmo dizer que é o reimaginar de um ícone, porque o LEAF carrega o título de “primeiro carro elétrico a ser produzido em massa”.

Lançado em 2010, conta com 700 mil unidades vendidas até à data, sendo que foi, durante vários anos, o elétrico mais popular do mundo. Contudo, a popularidade inicial foi desaparecendo e nem mesmo o anúncio da segunda geração, em 2018, conseguiu travar isso.

Agora, para recuperar esse protagonismo, a Nissan apostou numa fórmula diferente e mudou praticamente tudo para o novo LEAF, que aderiu ao formato crossover.

title: Nissan Leaf N Connecta Review 2020
description:
Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Review: A Comprehensive Look at the Affordable, Efficient Electric Vehicle

The Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 stands as one of the most popular and accessible electric vehicles (EVs) on the market today. With its environmentally friendly performance, stylish design, and tech-savvy features, the 2020 Nissan Leaf N-Connecta offers an exceptional blend of value, practicality, and sustainability. Whether you're making the switch to electric driving or looking for a reliable EV for city commuting and weekend road trips, the Nissan Leaf N-Connecta delivers a reasonable driving experience. This review will take a deep dive into the specs, features, and performance of the Leaf N-Connecta 2020 to help you determine if it's the right choice for your driving needs.

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020: Key Specifications

Battery Capacity: 40 kWh Lithium-ion
Motor Power: 110 kW (147 horsepower)
Range: Up to 168 miles on a full charge (WLTP)
Top Speed: 93 mph (150 km/h)
Acceleration (0-62 mph): 7.9 seconds
Charging Time (AC): Approximately 7.5 hours for a full charge (using a 7 kW charger)
Charging Time (DC): 40-60 minutes to charge from 0% to 80% (using a rapid charger)
Drive Type: Front-wheel drive (FWD)
CO2 Emissions: 0 g/km (emission-free)

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Driving Performance
When it comes to driving performance, the Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 provides a smooth and quiet ride, which is typical of electric vehicles. Powered by a 40 kWh lithium-ion battery and a 110 kW (147 horsepower) electric motor, the Leaf N-Connecta offers a decent balance of power and efficiency. The car can accelerate from 0 to 62 mph in just 7.9 seconds, which provides a responsive and engaging driving experience, especially in urban and suburban environments.

One standout feature is its e-Pedal system, which allows for one-pedal driving. By simply pressing and releasing the accelerator pedal, you can accelerate, decelerate, and come to a complete stop without using the brake pedal, providing a unique and efficient driving experience.

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Range and Charging
One of the key aspects of any electric vehicle is its driving range, and the Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 doesn't disappoint. The vehicle’s 40 kWh battery allows for a range of up to 168 miles on a full charge (WLTP), making it a practical option for daily commuting and even longer trips, especially if you're able to access rapid charging stations along the way.

For charging, the Leaf N-Connecta 2020 supports both AC and DC charging. Using a standard 7 kW home charger, the car can be fully charged in about 7.5 hours, making overnight charging convenient for most users. For faster charging, the Leaf is equipped with DC rapid charging capability, which can charge the battery from 0% to 80% in just 40-60 minutes, depending on the charging station.

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Technology and Safety Features
The Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 comes packed with a range of advanced technology and safety features. The NissanConnect infotainment system is intuitive, featuring an easy-to-use interface with 7-inch touchscreen functionality, Bluetooth connectivity, and smartphone integration through Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. The system allows drivers to access music, navigation, and contacts with ease, ensuring that you're always connected while on the road.

In terms of safety, the Leaf N-Connecta offers a suite of driver assistance features that contribute to a safe and enjoyable driving experience. Standard features include automatic emergency braking, lane departure warning, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert. The car is also equipped with ProPILOT, Nissan's semi-autonomous driving system, which offers adaptive cruise control, steering assistance, and lane centering for a more relaxed drive, especially on highways.

Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 Driving Experience
On the road, the Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 2020 offers a smooth and quiet ride, as you'd expect from an electric vehicle. The absence of engine noise makes for a calm and serene driving environment, and the car's precise steering and responsive acceleration make it enjoyable to drive. Whether you're navigating tight city streets or cruising on the highway, the Leaf N-Connecta feels composed and confident.

Conclusion
The Nissan Leaf offers a reasonably priced car that looks nice and drives way.
The main consideration with the Leaf is it's battery life. Will you be going on long journeys or holidays, sadly not. 
Will it go you to and from work and just about cover the primary function of a car, then yes.

We scored the Nissan Leaf N-Connecta 6/10

title: 2026 Nissan Leaf Fahrbericht Test Verbrauch Reichweite Ersteindruck | Electric Drive Check
description:
Der neue Nissan Leaf misst 4,35 Meter in der Länge, ohne Außenspiegel 1,81 Meter in der Breite und 1,55 Meter in der Höhe, der Radstand beträgt 2,69 Meter. In den Radhäusern drehen sich wahlweise 195/60 18", 215/55 R18" oder gar 235/45 R19" Räder. Unter der Karosserie, ich zitiere den Held der Steine, nichts vor denen man sich fürchten müsste, ganz im Gegenteil: MacPherson Federbeine vorne, Multilink Hinterachse. Bei der Karosserie selbst: Stromlinienförmige Gestaltung, bündig eingelassene Türgriffe, fließende Dachlinie.

Ihr habt die Qual der Wahl, es stehen zwei Batterieoptionen zur Verfügung: 52 kWh oder 75 kWh. Abhängig von der gewählten Option variiert auch die Peakleistung vom Elektromotor. 130 kW bei 52 kWh oder 160 kW bei 75 kWh. Das maximale Drehmoment liegt mit 345 bzw. 355 Nm fast auf einem Niveau und gleich bleibt stets die Höchstgeschwindigkeit, da wird der Nissan Leaf zugunsten der Reichweite nämlich bei 160 km/h eingebremst.Gleich dürfte auch die 30-Minuten-Dauerleistung sein, die bei diesem Elektromotor bei 70 kW liegen müsste.

Vervollständigen wir das Quartett-Spiel? Die Top-Version beschleunigt binnen 7,6 Sekunden von 0 auf 100 km/h, die Variante mit weniger Leistung benötigt 8,3 Sekunden für den Standard-Sprint und beim Gewicht bringt der neue Nissan Leaf der dritten Generation je nach Modell und Austattungs-Niveau zwischen 1.789 und 1.937 kg auf die Waage.

Was konnte schon der Nissan Leaf Vorgänger? Strom auch abgeben! Auch wenn Nissan aus guten Gründen im Nissan Leaf keinen ChaDeMo Anschluss mehr verwendet in Europa, besteht die Möglichkeit auch wieder Strom abzugeben mit maximal 3,6 kW über einen Vehicle to Load Adapter. 

Ladeleistungen? Bis zu 11 kW an AC, bis zu 105 kW bei der Variante mit 52 kWh und bis zu 150 kW bei der Variante mit dem großen Akku. Nissan verspricht uns, dass man den Ladezustand von 20-80% SoC jeweils in unter einer halben Stunde erhöhen kann, so soll man unter idealen Bedingungen in einer halben Stunde bei der Variante mit großem Akku bis zu 420 km Reichweite nachladen können, denn der WLTP-Wert wird mit 13,8 kWh / 100 km angegeben, die WLTP-Reichweite mit bis zu 622 km beim großen Akku, und bis zu 440 km bei der Variante mit kleinem Akku.  

Bei der ersten Testfahrt von Olli und Steffen hat der Nissan Leaf übrigens 16,4 kWh / 100 km verbraucht, Testdistanz 120 Kilometer, Durchschnittsgeschwindigkeit 48 km/h. Wir erinnern uns? 13,8 kWh/100 km gemäß WLTP, damit hat Olli auf der ersten Testfahrt um ca. 17,4 % überboten hat. Dabei muss man aber auch erwähnen, dass wir bei Dreharbeiten nicht immer besonderes effizient unterwegs sind. Was ich persönlich mag ist das One-Pedal-Driving und die Einstellbarkeit der Regnerationsstufen über die Schaltwippen. 

Das bringt uns nun zum Preis und obwohl Olli die Variante mit dem großen Akku gefahren ist, kann ich euch heute nur den Basispreis nennen von der Variante mit dem kleineren Akku und hier geht es los ab 37.000 Euro und darüber können wir nun fürstlich in der Kommentarspalte diskutieren.

Mit einem Luftwiderstandsbeiwert von 0,25 liegt der Leaf auf Augenhöhe mit teuren Premium-Elektroautos.

Das optionale Panoramadach trägt dezent den Schriftzug LEAF, und Felgen bis 19 Zoll im Aero-Design sorgen für den passenden Stand. Trotz kompakter Außenmaße mit 4,35 Metern Länge, 1,81 Metern Breite und 1,55 Metern Höhe bietet das Modell 437 Liter Kofferraumvolumen und damit familientaugliche Alltagsqualitäten.

Kundinnen und Kunden können zwischen zwei Batteriegrößen wählen, 52 kWh oder 75 kWh. Die kleinere Variante schafft rund 440 Kilometer nach WLTP, die größere sogar bis zu 622 Kilometer. Damit spielt der Leaf in einer Liga mit Modellen wie Tesla Model 3 oder Hyundai Ioniq 6. Bei 130 Kilometern pro Stunde bleibt die Reichweite mit rund 330 Kilometern beachtlich.

Geladen wird schnell. Bis zu 150 kW Gleichstrom sind möglich, was in rund 30 Minuten bis zu 440 Kilometer Reichweite nachlädt. Alternativ steht eine 11-kW-Wechselstromlösung bereit. Eine Besonderheit ist die Vehicle-to-Load-Funktion, kurz V2L, die bis zu 3,6 kW an externe Verbraucher abgeben kann. So lässt sich beim Camping sogar ein Elektrogrill betreiben.

Der neue Leaf basiert auf der CMF-EV-Plattform, die auch beim Nissan Ariya zum Einsatz kommt. Vorn arbeitet eine MacPherson-Federbeinachse, hinten eine Multilink-Konstruktion. Das sorgt für mehr Fahrkomfort und Stabilität. Der Elektromotor leistet 160 kW und 355 Nm Drehmoment, beschleunigt in 7,6 Sekunden auf 100 Kilometer pro Stunde und liefert ein agiles und leises Fahrerlebnis. In der Basisversion mit 52-kWh-Akku sind es 130 kW und 345 Nm.

Neben dem e-Pedal Step für Ein-Pedal-Fahren ist auch der ProPILOT Assistent mit Navi-Link an Bord, der auf der Autobahn automatisch Geschwindigkeit und Abstand regelt. Kameras und Sensoren liefern eine 3D-Rundumsicht inklusive Durchsicht durch die Motorhaube, was beim Einparken und Rangieren hilft.

Im Innenraum ist der Leaf ganz auf die digitale Zukunft vorbereitet. Zwei 14,3-Zoll-Displays verschmelzen zu einem durchgängigen Cockpit. Über das Infotainmentsystem NissanConnect mit integrierten Google-Diensten lassen sich Navigation, Klima und Medien per Sprachbefehl steuern. Google Maps übernimmt die Routenplanung inklusive Ladestopps, Google Play bringt Apps und Unterhaltung ins Auto.

Mit der NissanConnect Services App lässt sich das Fahrzeug aus der Ferne steuern. Besitzerinnen und Besitzer können den Batteriestatus prüfen, Ladevorgänge starten oder die Klimatisierung aktivieren, um das Auto vor Fahrtbeginn angenehm zu temperieren.

Gefertigt wird der neue Nissan Leaf im britischen Werk Sunderland, das zu 20 Prozent mit erneuerbarer Energie betrieben wird. Damit steht das Modell nicht nur für emissionsfreies Fahren, sondern auch für nachhaltige Produktion.

title: 2025 Nissan Leaf Concept: The Silent Storm of Japanese Innovation
description:
The future whispers—and the 2025 Nissan Leaf Concept answers with the grace of a katana slicing through the wind. This isn’t just an electric car; it’s a manifesto of Japanese precision, wrapped in a shell so sleek it seems to defy physics.  

#### Visually Arresting Exterior  
Gone are the meek curves of its predecessors—this Leaf wears a suit of liquid obsidian, its LED blade-lights pulsing like a cyborg’s heartbeat. The floating C-pillar and retractable rear spoiler aren’t just design flourishes; they’re aerodynamic witchcraft, cutting drag to a whisper.  

#### Pioneering Interior Innovations  
Slide inside, and the cabin hums with minimalist futurism. A panoramic OLED dash curves like a samurai’s bow, projecting holographic navigation onto the windshield. The seats, woven from upcycled ocean plastics, cradle you like a zero-gravity throne. And the AI co-pilot? It doesn’t just respond—it anticipates, adjusting climate and playlist before you even sigh.  

#### State-of-the-Art Performance  
Powered by Nissan’s next-gen e-4ORCE dual-motor setup (248 hp, 340 lb-ft), the Leaf Concept sprints from 0–100 km/h in 5.9 seconds—silent, but deadly. The solid-state battery grants 380 miles of range, recharging in 15 minutes flat at ultra-fast stations.  

#### Market Adversaries & Competitive Edge  
The Tesla Model 3 and Hyundai Ioniq 6 loom large, but the Leaf counters with better weight distribution, lower maintenance costs, and a near-silent ride that feels like gliding on magnetic rails.  

#### Pricing & Value Proposition  
Starting at $42,500, it undercuts Tesla while offering superior build quality and Nissan’s legendary reliability. Resale? Strong, thanks to battery longevity guarantees.

title: 🚗✨2026 Toyota Corolla First Look – Can This Sedan Rival The Honda Civic Again
description:
The 2026 Toyota Corolla is imagined as the next generation of one of the world’s best-selling cars, carrying forward more than 50 years of reputation for reliability, efficiency, and everyday usability. Since its debut in 1966, the Corolla has evolved into a global icon, available in sedan, hatchback, and hybrid variants. For 2026, Toyota is expected to push the Corolla further into electrification, enhance its technology, and refine its design to remain a leader in the compact car segment against rivals like the Honda Civic, Mazda3, Hyundai Elantra, and Nissan Sentra.

Exterior design
The 2026 Corolla would likely adopt a sharper and more dynamic look, inspired by Toyota’s latest design language seen in recent Prius and Crown models. Expect slimmer LED headlights, a reworked grille, and more aerodynamic sculpting to improve efficiency. Hatchback versions may emphasize a sportier profile with bold lines and coupe-like elements, while the sedan would retain its refined, professional appeal. Alloy wheels in 16–18 inch sizes would reinforce its stylish yet practical stance.

Interior and comfort
Inside, the 2026 Corolla is expected to deliver a blend of simplicity, durability, and advanced features. A wide digital instrument cluster, large central infotainment system, and wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto would come standard. Higher trims may include leather seating, ambient lighting, and premium audio systems. Toyota’s ergonomic focus would ensure generous comfort in both rows, while foldable rear seats in the hatchback variant would add extra practicality.

Rear styling and practicality
At the rear, the 2026 Corolla sedan could adopt slimmer LED taillamps and a sculpted trunk design, while the hatchback might feature sportier details like a roof spoiler and a more aggressive bumper. Both would emphasize modern styling without compromising functionality.

Wheels and stance
With 16–18 inch alloys, the 2026 Corolla would balance efficiency with a more athletic presence. A slightly wider stance and lower profile may also improve aerodynamics and driving stability.

Powertrain and performance
Toyota is expected to expand electrification in the Corolla lineup. Options may include:

A 1.8L or 2.0L hybrid system, refined for improved performance and efficiency.

A plug-in hybrid (PHEV) model offering extended electric-only driving range.

A potential Corolla EV variant for selected markets, competing with compact EVs like the Nissan Leaf and Hyundai Ioniq 5.

Gasoline-only models may remain in some regions, but hybrids are likely to dominate the lineup. Driving dynamics would continue to improve with Toyota’s TNGA platform, ensuring agility and ride comfort.

Market positioning
The 2026 Toyota Corolla would continue to serve as a reliable, efficient, and affordable compact car for global markets. With electrified options and modern tech, it would compete strongly against the Honda Civic, Mazda3, Hyundai Elantra, Nissan Sentra, and even premium compacts like the VW Golf. Positioned as both practical and stylish, it would remain one of the most versatile cars worldwide.

Rock crawling is an extreme form of off-road driving using specialized vehicles ranging from stock to highly modified, to overcome obstacles. In rock crawling, drivers typically drive highly modified four-wheel-drive vehicles such as trucks, Jeeps, and "buggies" over very harsh terrain. Driving locations include boulders, mountain foothills, rock piles, mountain trails, etc.

Rock crawling is about slow-speed, careful and precise driving, and high torque generated through large gear reductions (100:1 or more) in the vehicle's drivetrain. Rock crawlers often drive up, down and across obstacles that appear impassable.

Rock crawling competitions range from local events to national series. These consist of 100–200-yard (91–183 m) long courses with obstacles set up with gates, similar to a slalom ski race.

Vehicles commonly used include Jeep (the Chrysler and the Mitsubishi Varieties), Lada Niva, BAW, Nissan Patrol, Toyota Hilux, Toyota Land Cruiser, Land Rover, Mercedes-Benz G-Class, Santana PS-10, Ford Bronco, Suzuki Samurai, International Scout among many other 4x4's. These vehicles are outfitted with custom parts. Rock Crawlers can be built by a wide array of companies as well as in people's garages. Power is usually not an issue, as rock crawlers typically lower their gear ratios in order to drive more slowly over obstacles without stalling the engine. These custom parts can include:

locking differentials
taller off-road tires
upgraded suspension
four wheel steering
heavy duty steering components/solid front axle
roll cage for driver protection
lowered gearing in either or all of the transmission, transfer case (including often employing a second transfer case to reduce gearing even more), or axle differentials
winches
barwork (bullbar, rock sliders, brush bars, rear bar/tyre carrier and/or external roll cage bolted or welded to frame)
armour (protects exposed underbody components: radiator, engine oil sump, driveline)
beadlocks (locks tires to the rims for low tire pressures)
long-travel shock absorbers, drop shackles, spring-over conversions (to increase wheel travel), coil-over spring/shock combinations, and upgraded control arms
portal axles
Oversized, low-pressure, knobby, mud-terrain tires are used. Most vehicles have a low-geared transfer case to make the most torque in the low speeds used for rock crawling. Suspension-wise, rock crawling vehicles sometimes have after-market lift kits installed, raising the chassis and increasing suspension flex, though the rock crawlers running the tougher trails often have fabricated suspension systems, or home-assembled leaf packs to cheaply achieve the goals, making it easier to drive over larger obstacles with less risk of damage to the vehicle. Most suspensions are made to be highly flexible, allowing for the maximum amount of tire area to contact the ground, while keeping the vehicle as low as possible. Due to the conflicting nature of the dynamics and needs of rock crawling and highway driving vehicles, it is not unusual to modify a vehicle solely for off-road recreational usage.

Once a vehicle is deemed "off-road only" i.e. not driven on the street and trailered to trails or OHV parks (Off-Highway Vehicle), then the modification possibilities are endless.

description:

It’s time for an all-new EV range test! 

We’ve got our hands on some of the latest all-electric SUVs, and we’re going to compare them to not only see which will go the furthest, but also how close each of them will get to their claimed range! 

The contenders we have today are the Genesis GV70, BMW iX, Polestar 3, Audi Q6 e-tron, and the Kia EV9. Let’s take a closer look at the contenders. 

The Genesis GV70 rolls up with an 80kWh battery pack and two electric motors. These combine to produce 490hp and 700Nm, and the GV70 has a claimed range of 298 miles. Picking one up new costs around £66,000. 

The BMW iX also has two motors, and they combine to produce 544hp and 765Nm. It has a larger battery than the GV70, though, at 109kWh, so as a result it has a much larger claimed range - 426 miles. It costs a whole lot more, though, with the car we have for this video costing £107,000! 

The Audi Q6 e-tron starts from £61,000, but for the exact car we have here, it costs from £71,000! Unlike the previous two cars, it only has one electric motor, and this produces 306hp and 485Nm. It has a claimed range of 360 miles, and a 95kWh battery pack.

Up next is the Kia EV9. The exact car we have here only costs from £65,000, and like the Audi it only has a single motor which is good for 203hp and 350Nm. It’s also equipped with a 100kWh battery, and this is good for a claimed range of 349 miles.

Then, finally, we have the Polestar 3. The car here is the entry-level model, which starts from around £70,000, but it has some optional extras added to it, so this car here costs around £85,000. It’s equipped with a single motor for 300hp and 490Nm. There’s a 111kWh battery pack, which gives the Polestar a claimed range of 438 miles.

title: Tata Nexon EV vs MG Windsor EV!
description:
The Tata Nexon EV is a sub-4 metre electric SUV that has been extremely popular in the Indian market. It first went on sale in 2020 and later down the line, got a heavily revised facelift in 2023. The Nexon EV brings power, silence and lower running costs to what is an already capable car in its ICE avatar.

The MG Windsor EV is an electric crossover in India and offers the seating capacity for up to five people. The Windsor EV is the third all-electric from MG India after the ZS EV and Comet EV. It uses a 38 kWh battery and offers a claimed range of up to 331 km. The Windsor EV blends practicality with a well-appointed interior and a comprehensive suite of features.

title: New 2026 Suzuki e-Vitara Vs 2026 Hyundai Creta EV The Brand's First Fully EV Comparison
description:
The #2026-Suzuki-e-Vitara and the #2026-Hyundai-Creta-EV mark a major shift for both brands as their first global, mass-market electric SUVs. While the #e-Vitara is a "born-electric" vehicle built on a dedicated EV platform (Heartect-e), the #Creta-EV is an electric conversion of the popular internal combustion engine (ICE) Creta.
Key Features:
#Suzuki Highlights: 10-way power-adjustable driver seat, 18-inch wheels, 7 airbags, and "Snow" terrain mode.
#Hyundai Highlights: Panoramic sunroof, dual-zone climate control, "Boss Mode" (moving the front passenger seat from the rear), and Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) technology, which allows you to power external appliances from the car's battery.
Verdict:
The #Suzuki-e-Vitara is arguably the better choice for those seeking a dedicated EV platform with genuine off-road capability (AWD) and a lower entry price. The #Hyundai-Creta-EV is geared toward buyers who prioritize premium features, faster charging, and the familiarity and interior space of the standard Creta.
Price and Variants:
Maruti #Suzuki-e-Vitara:
Price: ₹15.99 Lakh to ₹20.01 Lakh.
BaaS: ₹10.99 Lakh + ₹3.99/km.
3 Variants: Delta, Zeta, Alpha.
#Hyundai-Creta Electric:
Price: ₹18.02 L to ₹24.40 L.
Variants: Executive, Smart, Premium, Excellence
Verdict: The prices of the Maruti #Suzuki-e-Vitara makes it highly affordable, compared to the #Hyundai-Creta-EV.
Final Selection Guide:
Choose the #Suzuki-e-Vitara if: You want the lowest possible entry price via BaaS, require AWD for light off-roading or snowy conditions, or value a dedicated EV platform with a longer wheelbase.

title: Фінський стартап Donut Lab зробив твердотільну батарею для мотоциклів Verge. В чому її унікальність?
description:
Розпочнемо із компанії, яка таки досягнула бажаного результату, попри всі сумніви скептиків. Принаймні, вона так заявляє. Перший мотоцикл з твердотільною батареєю зійшов з конвеєра! 
Фінсько-естонський виробник мотоциклів Verge в останні кілька років часто з’являвся в заголовках новин зі своїми інноваціями для байків. Інновації були створені переважно його партнерською компанією Donut Lab, про яку частина з вас могла чути завдяки їх революційним двигунам “пончикам”, які встановлюються прямо в колесо (власне, тому і дОнат), і обіцянкам випустити на ринок твердотільні батареї. І, схоже, компанія нарешті отримала в цьому напрямку варті уваги досягнення.
Днями Donut Lab оприлюднила результати своїх перших випробувань заряджання на рівні всього акумуляторного блоку — це вже четвертий тест батареї спільно з Verge Motorcycles. Їхній блок ємністю 18 кВт⋅год підтримував потужність заряджання понад 100 кВт при швидкості 5C (5 сі), що є абсолютно екстремальною швидкістю для звичайних літій-іонних батарей, протягом п’яти хвилин на електромотоциклі Verge TS Pro.
Те, що твердотільна батарея Donut Lab витримала 5C протягом 5 хвилин (і зарядилася з 10% до 50% за цей час) без рідинного охолодження — це революційний показник. Це означає, що їхня хімія здатна «перетравлювати» величезну потужність дуже швидко і без критичних наслідків для структури акумулятора. 
Простими словами: 5C — це режим «супер-швидкої зарядки», який дозволяє заповнити значну частину баку, поки ви просто купуєте каву на заправці.
До речі, для порівняння: більшість сучасних електромобілів (навіть Tesla) зазвичай заряджаються на швидкості від 1C до 3C у пікових моментах. Показник 5C — це вже територія технологій майбутнього.

title: Xiaomi YU7 PRO или Tesla Model Y. Что лучше КУПИТЬ, если бюджет не резиновый? Тест-драйв. Обзор
description:
Когда в прошлом году мы привезли первую Xiaomi YU7 в версии Мах - не было смысла сравнивать ее с Tesla Model Y. Новинка от производителя телефонов и пылесосов была мощнее и дороже. Но с появлением версии Pro все изменилось. Теперь это прямой конкурент Tesla Model Y, как минимум по цене. А в остальном? А вот все остальное мы и сравнили.

Китайский новичок обещает 770 км запаса, пневмоподвеску и салон с намёком на роскошь. Американский ветеран — идеальный баланс управляемости и комфорта плюс лучшую инфраструктуру. Кто победит? Я провёл день за рулём обеих машин, чтобы узнать правду.

Что скрывают тест-драйвы:
Почему Tesla с меньшим запасом хода ощущается динамичнее
Где Xiaomi реально выигрывает (спойлер: мягкость и размеры)
В чём американская машина остаётся королём (ремонт, софт, запчасти)
Правда о «заводском русском языке» и «английском, который не перевести»

Вы увидите шокирующие детали:
Как багажники отличаются в реальной жизни, а не на бумаге
Почему выдвижные ручки скоро запретят в Китае (и что это значит для безопасности)
Чьё приложение удобнее — Tesla или Xiaomi (спойлер: отрыв огромный)
Стоят ли 770 км запаса ваших нервов с китайской экосистемой

P.S.: В финале — честный вердикт: кому брать Xiaomi, а кому бежать к Tesla. И да, мы разрешили голосование в комментариях — так что победителя выберете вы.

title: Tata Harrier Ev vs Mahindra BE 6 | Real comparison! No hype!
description:
Tata Harrier Ev vs Mahindra BE 6 | Real comparison! No hype!

अगर आप EV की दुनिया में धमाल मचाने की प्लानिंग कर रहे हैं, तो ज़रूर ये वीडियो देखिए! 🚗⚡

इस वीडियो में हम ले कर आए हैं Tata Harrier EV और Mahindra BE 6 का दमदार मुकाबला — पावर, परफॉर्मेंस, स्पेस, स्टाइल, चार्जिंग और फीचर्स सभी एंगल्स से। जानिए क्यों Harrier EV का ड्यूल मोटर AWD वैरिएंट रॉ थ्रिल और ऑफ‑रोड मांसपावर में सबसे आगे खड़ी है, और क्या BE 6 का कूप-स्पोर्टी लुक, बड़ा फ्रंक, बेहतर चार्जिंग और फ्यूचरिस्टिक केबिन आपकी शहरी जिंदगी के लिए बेस्ट चॉइस हो सकती है। इस वीडियो में शामिल है:

🔹 Dimensional showdown
🔹 Battery & real-world range comparison
🔹 Powerplay: bhp & torque face‑off
🔹 Charging ecosystems tested
🔹 Feature highlights & cabin experience
🔹 Build-quality & safety verdict

तो अगर आप “टफ एंड टॉर्क… या टेक और लग्ज़री?” में उलझे हुए हैं, तो यह वीडियो आपकी क्विक गाइड बन सकती है! 👊🔥

ऑल-व्हील ड्राइव (AWD): क्या Harrier EV का ये फीचर आपको ज़्यादा ऑफ-रोड एडवेंचर की ओर आकर्षित करता है?

डायमेंशन और स्पेस: क्या आप थोड़ी मस्कुलर लेआउट (Harrier EV) में अधिक कंफर्ट पसंद करेंगे, या लंबा व्हीलबेस और बूट स्पेस (BE 6) को प्राथमिकता देंगे?

रेंज के मामले में एफिशिएंसी: क्या BE 6 की बैटरी एफिशिएंसी आपको Harrier EV से कहीं ज़्यादा आकर्षित करती है?

परफॉर्मेंस और पावर: क्या 390 bhp और 504 Nm torque वाले Harrier EV AWD वेरिएंट का ड्राइविंग एक्सपीरियंस आप देखने के लिए उत्साहित हैं?

चार्जिंग स्पीड: क्या आपको BE 6 के 180 kW DC & 11.2 kW AC चार्जिंग पॉइंट ज़्यादा दिलचस्प लगते हैं, खासकर लंबी दूरी के सफरों के लिए?

स्टाइल और लुक: आप कौनसा लुक ज़्यादा पसंद करेंगे — Robotic, muscular SUV जैसा Harrier EV या futuristic coupe-स्पोर्टी BE 6?

Namaste doston! Aaj ke is detailed video me hum baat karne wale hain Mahindra XEV 9S ke baare me — ek modern, futuristic aur India ki sabse affordable 7-seater electric SUV. Is video me hum is car ka exterior, interior, battery options, range, performance, safety features, expected service experience, customer review points, price aur last me mera honest opinion complete detail me cover karenge.

⚡ ABOUT MAHINDRA XEV 9S  
Mahindra XEV 9S INGLO EV platform par based hai, jo ek lightweight, safe aur advanced EV architecture provide karta hai. Ye car futuristic design, tech-loaded cabin, long range aur 7-seater practicality ke saath aati hai, jo family buyers ke liye perfect option ban sakti hai.

🚗 EXTERIOR DETAILS  
XEV 9S ka exterior kaafi stylish aur modern approach follow karta hai.  
Slim LED DRLs, closed EV grille, sporty bumper, aerodynamic bodylines, flush door handles aur connected LED tail lights is car ko ek premium EV look dete hain.  
Large alloy wheels aur upright SUV stance iski road presence ko kaafi strong banate hain.

🏠 INTERIOR & FEATURES  
Interior minimal, clean aur tech-focused design ke saath aata hai.  
Dual-screen setup, digital instrument cluster, ambient lighting, wireless charging, large sunroof, flat floor design aur spacious 7-seater cabin is gaadi ko family-friendly banate hain.  
Boot space aur seating comfort long drives aur city usage, dono ke liye suitable hai.

🔋 BATTERY, MOTOR & RANGE  
Mahindra XEV 9S me expected battery options 59 kWh, 70 kWh aur 79 kWh reh sakte hain.  
Range approx 450–500 km tak mil sakti hai, variant ke hisab se.  
Fast charging support se 30–35 minutes me 80% charging possible hogi.  
Instant torque aur smooth EV performance city aur highway dono me comfortable driving experience degi.

🛡 SAFETY FEATURES  
Mahindra safety ke liye famous brand hai.  
Expected safety package:  
• 6–7 Airbags  
• ABS + ESC  
• Hill Assist  
• TPMS  
• 360° Camera  
• Advanced ADAS Level 2  
• Strong EV structure with good crash safety

🛠 SERVICE EXPERIENCE  
Mahindra apni EV service network ko rapidly expand kar rahi hai.  
Metro cities me charging + service support easily available ho raha hai.  
EV platform ke saath maintenance cost kaafi low rehne wali hai.

💰 PRICE & LAUNCH  
Expected price approx ₹19–22 lakh ke beech.  
Launch 2025 end ya 2026 shuruaat me expected hai.

⭐ CUSTOMER REVIEW STYLE POV  
Users ko is car ki design, feature list, range aur 7-seater practicality sabse zyada pasand aa sakti hai.  
Family usage, long trips aur daily commute ke liye ye ek balanced EV option lagti hai.

✨ MY HONEST OPINION  
Mahindra XEV 9S ek promising electric 7-seater SUV banne wali hai.  
Agar aap futuristic, feature-loaded, long range EV ek family car ke form me dhoondh rahe ho to ye definitely wait karne layak car hai.

While it shares its foundation with the Toyota Highlander EV, the Getaway distinguishes itself with a more aggressive exterior design, plus it has 8.3 inches of ground clearance and heavy-duty roof rails capable of supporting a rooftop tent.
Inside, this electric Subaru SUV feels more premium than anything else in the current Subaru lineup. The top-tier trims feature Nappa leather, as well as a 14-inch touchscreen interface that far surpasses the tech found in the current Subaru Forester or Outback. Space is a major highlight, too; the long wheelbase provides an impressively roomy third row and a flat load floor for cargo.
Performance-wise, the Getaway aims to be a strong player in the electric 3-row SUV segment. Every trim comes standard with all-wheel drive and a potent 420-horsepower powertrain, allowing for a 0-60 mph sprint in under 5 seconds. Subaru estimates over 300 miles of range from a 95.8 kWh battery, and the inclusion of a NACS port ensures easy access to the Tesla Supercharger network. While pricing isn't official, Subaru is positioning the Getaway to be a high-value alternative to rivals like the Kia EV9 and Hyundai Ioniq 9, and we estimate a price point starting in the $60,000 range.

title: Vayve Eva: India’s First Solar-Powered Electric Car Launched at ₹3.25 Lakh | Features & Details
description:
India has taken a significant leap in sustainable transportation with the launch of the Vayve Eva, the nation’s first solar-powered electric car. Unveiled at the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025, the Eva is set to revolutionize urban mobility with its compact design, eco-friendly technology, and affordability.  ￼

Design and Dimensions

The Vayve Eva is reminiscent of small EVs like the Mahindra E2O and Reva, featuring a compact hatchback design ideal for city commutes. It measures 2,950 mm in length and 1,200 mm in width, making it adept at navigating through congested urban areas. Despite its petite size, the Eva comfortably accommodates up to two adults and one child, providing a practical solution for small families or individual travelers.  ￼

Variants and Pricing

Vayve offers the Eva in three variants to cater to diverse customer needs:
 • Nova: Priced at ₹3.25 lakh (ex-showroom), this base model comes with a 9 kWh battery pack, delivering a real-world range of approximately 125 km.  ￼
 • Stella: At ₹3.99 lakh (ex-showroom), the Stella variant is equipped with a 12.6 kWh battery, offering a range of around 175 km.  ￼
 • Vega: The top-tier Vega variant is priced at ₹4.49 lakh (ex-showroom) and features an 18 kWh battery pack, providing an impressive range of up to 250 km on a single charge.  ￼

Solar Integration and Charging

A standout feature of the Eva is its solar roof, capable of providing an additional range of up to 10 km per day, translating to approximately 3,000 km of free driving annually. This solar integration reduces dependency on charging infrastructure, promoting a more sustainable mode of transportation. For conventional charging, the Eva supports DC fast charging, allowing the battery to reach 80% capacity in just 45 minutes.  ￼

Performance and Specifications

The Eva is powered by an electric motor delivering 20.11 bhp, ensuring efficient performance for urban driving. Its compact dimensions and lightweight design contribute to an operational cost of approximately ₹0.5 per km, making it an economical choice for daily commutes.  ￼

Interior and Features

Inside, the Eva is equipped with modern amenities to enhance the driving experience. Features include dual digital displays, a 6-way powered driver seat, and a fixed glass roof, providing a blend of comfort and convenience. The vehicle also offers smart connectivity options, including Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, ensuring drivers stay connected on the go.  ￼

Safety Features

Safety is a priority in the Eva’s design. The vehicle comes with a driver airbag and seatbelts for both passengers, providing essential protection during city drives. Additionally, the monocoque chassis and front crumple zone enhance the vehicle’s safety credentials.  ￼

Conclusion

The Vayve Eva represents a significant advancement in India’s electric vehicle landscape, offering an affordable, eco-friendly, and practical solution for urban transportation. Its combination of solar integration, compact design, and modern features positions it as a compelling choice for environmentally conscious consumers. With pre-launch bookings set to open in January 2025, the Eva is poised to make a substantial impact on the Indian automotive market.
