Welcome back to Adi Zone, and today we’re exploring one of the most talked-about electric SUVs of 2025 — the VinFast VF6! 🌟 This compact EV from Vietnam is setting a new benchmark in design, performance, and technology. In this detailed ownership review, we bring you the complete experience — from the first drive to daily use, range performance, features, and real-world impressions.

🚘 Design & Road Presence

The VinFast VF6 turns heads with its futuristic styling, sharp LED signature lights, aerodynamic silhouette, and bold stance. Whether you see it from the front or the rear, it has a unique identity that sets it apart from any other EV in its segment. The build quality feels solid, and the paint finish is premium — easily comparable to global competitors like Hyundai Kona EV or MG ZS EV.

🛋️ Interior & Comfort

Step inside the VF6 and you’re greeted by a minimalist yet high-tech cabin. The dashboard is dominated by a large central touchscreen with a clean layout and responsive UI. The absence of a traditional instrument cluster gives it a futuristic vibe, while the panoramic glass roof, ambient lighting, and premium upholstery elevate the driving experience.
Rear passengers get excellent legroom and under-thigh support, making long journeys comfortable. The boot space is practical enough for city errands and weekend getaways alike.

⚙️ Performance & Driving Experience

Under the hood, the VF6 offers instant torque and a smooth power delivery typical of EVs. The steering is light in the city but gains weight at higher speeds, giving you confidence on highways. Suspension tuning is spot-on — comfortable over rough roads yet stable around corners.
Whether you’re driving in Eco or Sport mode, the VF6 delivers a refined and silent experience, making every ride effortless.

🔋 Range & Charging

In real-world conditions, the VinFast VF6 delivers around 350–400 km of range, depending on driving style and conditions. Fast charging can take the battery from 20% to 80% in just about 35 minutes, making it ideal for daily commutes and even outstation trips. VinFast’s growing charging network is an added advantage, especially as they expand across India.

📱 Technology & Features

The VF6 is loaded with smart connectivity — including wireless Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, voice commands, over-the-air (OTA) updates, and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). Safety is a big highlight, with features like lane keep assist, adaptive cruise control, collision warning, and automatic emergency braking.

🧾 Ownership Experience

As an owner, the VF6 feels not just like a car — but like a connected, intelligent mobility partner. The after-sales service and warranty packages offered by VinFast are comprehensive, ensuring peace of mind. The battery warranty and regular software updates keep the car feeling fresh even years after purchase.

💬 Verdict

The VinFast VF6 combines futuristic design, cutting-edge technology, and practical performance in one affordable EV package. It’s an ideal choice for urban families, young professionals, and EV enthusiasts who want to step into the future of mobility without compromise.

If you’re planning to buy your first electric SUV, the VF6 deserves to be on your shortlist. It’s stylish, efficient, and built with precision — a true showcase of VinFast’s global ambitions. 🌍✨

Chery has unveiled its next-generation Rhino solid-state battery that could deliver more than 1,500 km of driving range on a single charge. The company says the battery is targeting an energy density of up to 600 Wh/kg, which is far higher than current lithium-ion batteries used in most EVs today.

One of the biggest highlights is ultra-fast charging. Chery claims the Rhino battery can add up to 500 km of range in just 8 minutes. The battery is also designed for around 5,000 charging cycles, which could make it last much longer than current EV batteries.

Chery plans to begin testing the all-solid-state battery in the Exeed ES8 from 2027. Before that, semi-solid-state versions are expected to debut in other Chery and Exeed models later in 2026.

The Rhino battery family includes hybrid, fully electric, and future solid-state versions. Chery is investing heavily in this technology with more than 1,200 battery researchers and over RMB 10 billion in funding.

We got our hands on the elusive Geely M9, a three-row family SUV built in China and currently unavailable in North America. If you've never heard of it, pay attention, because this luxury SUV is packed with tech that should put every automaker on notice. The Galaxy M9 isn't just a standard Chinese EV; it’s an advanced plug-in hybrid SUV featuring a turbocharged 1.5-liter engine that acts as a generator for its battery pack.
Performance-wise, the Geely M9 boasts three electric motors producing a combined 850 horsepower. At our test track, it rocketed from 0 to 60 mph in just 4.2 seconds — wildly quick for a vehicle weighing nearly 5,800 pounds. But the real jaw-dropper is its range. Geely says this plug-in hybrid can travel 130 miles on electricity alone — more than any PHEV sold in America — and an astonishing 808 miles with a full tank and charged battery. Inside, the cabin rivals the best in class, featuring a massive 30-inch 6K display, ultra-comfortable massaging seats, and even a built-in fridge.
The Geely M9 price is perhaps the most shocking part. In China, this fully loaded model goes for around $35,000. While tariffs and other costs would likely see that number skyrocket if this SUV ever arrived in the U.S., Chinese cars like the Geely M9 prove that automakers globally need to step up their game. For now, this forbidden 3-row SUV remains a fascinating glimpse into the future of automotive tech.

title: My new daily is NOT what you expect
description:
Get 20% off Car Vertical using code Carwow: https://bit.ly/Carwow-Car-Vertical

Has Mat finally lost the plot? This week on Carwow, we’ve added one of the rarest cars in the UK to the fleet: the Mia C. It’s a tiny, French electric car built between 2011 and 2013 that is actually rarer than a Ferrari F40! Only 1,000 were ever made before the company went bust.

With only 11 registered on UK roads, Mat sets out to discover if this central-seat micro-car is a misunderstood genius or a total waste of money!

So what exactly is the Mia C? Unlike the Citroën Ami, the Mia C is classified as an actual car, meaning you can drive it on motorways. It features:
- McLaren F1 Layout: A three-seat configuration with the driver positioned in the centre.
- Bizarre Entry: No traditional door handles! You have to press the flower logo to release the electric latch for the sliding doors.
- Performance (or lack thereof): With a choice of 8kWh or 12kWh batteries, it’s "supposed" to have a range of up to 78 miles.

And as you can imagine, it wouldn't be a Carwow video without some punishment. Mat puts the Mia through:
- Real-world Range Test: We drive it until the battery dies to see how close it gets to its 13-year-old promises.
- Performance Testing: Mat records the slowest 0-60 mph time in Carwow history - a staggering 56.49 seconds!
- The Braking Disaster: An emergency stop reveals that the ABS is completely broken, leading to a terrifying 209-foot braking distance! After this, he took a trip straight to the mechanics…

And the trip to the mechanics led to more problems - the struggle to find parts for such a rare car! Mat discovers that many components, such as the rear shock absorbers, were made by companies that build parts for fighter jets and are nearly impossible to source. After failing to use AI to find parts, Mat tracks down specialists in Germany and someone in the UK who actually recognises this specific car from its past life, and helps to get it MOT-ready!

After spending over £1,600 just to get it through an MOT, Mat takes the Mia to Topaz for a complete makeover. The question is, how good will the final edition of the Mia C look? And more importantly, will Mat finally be happy with his purchase? You’ll need to stick around and see for yourself!

Meet the BYD Seal U! 

It’s a family-friendly SUV from China, and it comes with a starting price of just £33,315! 

The question is, does it offer enough to steer you away from more established, well-known brands like Nissan and the ever-popular Qashqai? Let’s take a closer look… 

Starting with the design, there’s no denying that the Seal U looks pretty smart on the outside. The front end is well designed, with the DRLs positioned under the main headlights, while a large slatted grille gives the car a good presence. Along the side, there’s a bold crease running along the width of the car, while there’s also lots of chrome trim around the windows and the door sills. There’s only one choice of alloy wheel design available, but it looks pretty smart. Around the back, there’s a full-length light bar, and there are lots of layers from the top down to the bottom. All-in, it looks relatively smart. 

The interior of the Seal U is generally well-made. It comes with lots of soft-touch materials throughout, and the seats are covered in leatherette and are both heated and cooled! There’s a huge infotainment screen in the middle of the dash (which can rotate!), and the system is super-responsive and easy to use. It also comes with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as standard. There’s a large digital dial screen as well as a heads-up display, and there’s a good amount of storage throughout the cabin.

In terms of engines, every version of the Seal U is a plug-in hybrid. The entry-level car has a 1.5-litre petrol engine coupled with an electric motor, as well as an 18.3kWh battery, and it can produce 218hp. The next car up has the same engine and single motor, but a bigger 26.6kWh battery to allow for further driving on electric power alone. This version also delivers 218hp. The range-topping Seal U adds a turbocharger to the 1.5-litre engine, and it also adds an additional motor for all-wheel drive. The motors and engine combine to produce 324hp. 

So while the entry-level Seal U costs £33,315, the price rises to £40,015 for the range-topper. So is it worth it? You’ll need to stick with Mat to see for yourself!

This is the all-new Renault 5! 

The original Renault 5 was released in the 1970s, but it went out of production way back in 1996. However, it’s now been resurrected in the form of an EV! The question, does the new Renault 5 do justice to the legacy of its predecessors? Let’s take a closer look…

Starting with the exterior design, there’s no denying that Renault has got it bang on! It’s modern yet retro, with several design cues taken from the design of the original Renault 5. Along the side, you get contrasting side mirrors and skirts, and there are different colour roofs available as well! At the back, there are contoured tail lights and fake vents that harp back to the Turbo 2. 

The retro-modern style continues through to the interior. There’s a dual digital dial-infotainment screen on the dash that looks smart and integrated, while there’s a striped design across the rest of the dash to help give it some definition. There may be some hard, scratchy plastics within the cabin, but you have to remember this is still an entry-level car. Thankfully, there’s also a selection of physical buttons on the centre console! The seats not only look retro and cool, but they’re comfortable as well! 

There are two power output choices for the Renault 5. The entry-level is the Urban, which delivers 120hp, 225Nm, and has a claimed 0-60 time of 9 seconds. It also has a claimed range of up to 190 miles. Then we have the Comfort, which delivers 150hp, 245Nm, and a 0-60 time of 7.9 seconds. The claimed range of this edition is 248 miles.

The entry-level Renault 5 starts at £23,000, rising to £29,000 for the range-topping edition. So is it the best small electric car you can buy for under £30,000? You’ll need to stick with Mat and see for yourself!

The 2025 Leapmotor C10 is already doubling down on its attack on Australia's mid-size SUV segment with a new powertrain option, dubbed REEV. It stands for Range Extending Electric Vehicle, meaning it introduces an internal-combustion engine to extend the driving range of the otherwise fully electric car.

Confused? Don't be. The new C10 REEV combines a 1.5-litre petrol four-cylinder unit with a 158kW electric motor. The former acts as a power generator for the 28.4kWh battery pack that can also be charged via a plug, while the latter exclusively drives the wheels. The end result is a NEDC-rated driving range of 1150km and an average fuel consumption of just 0.9L/100km.

In this expert review, CarsGuide Contributing Journalist Byron Mathioudakis travels to Spain to get an early taste of the C10 REEV before it arrives Down Under. Point being, is it worth waiting for over a BYD Sealion 6 PHEV? Watch on to find out.

title: o carro elétrico BRASILEIRO
description:
O Gurgel Itaipu foi o primeiro carro elétrico da América Latina, lançado pela empresa brasileira Gurgel em 1974.  O projeto original, o Itaipu E150, era um microcarro com carroceria de fibra de vidro, projetado para dois passageiros, com autonomia de 60 a 80 km e velocidade máxima de 50 km/h, mas ficou restrito à fase de protótipos devido a limitações tecnológicas da época, como o alto custo e o peso das baterias de chumbo-ácido. 

Anos depois, em 1981, a Gurgel lançou o Itaipu E400, que se tornou o primeiro carro elétrico brasileiro fabricado em série.  Diferente do E150, o E400 era um utilitário baseado na estrutura da Volkswagen Kombi, com carroceria de plástico reforçado, disponível nas versões furgão e picape (simples e dupla), com capacidade de carga de 400 kg e autonomia de até 80 a 127 km.  O modelo foi produzido entre 1981 e 1982, com cerca de 76 unidades vendidas principalmente para empresas estatais e privadas que buscavam veículos econômicos para uso urbano. 

Ambos os modelos foram pioneiros em sua época, antecipando a tendência de eletrificação que só ganharia força global décadas mais tarde. O E150 foi apresentado no Salão do Automóvel de 1974, enquanto o E400 foi desenvolvido para atender a um desafio da Eletrobras, utilizando um motor elétrico de 10 kW (13,6 cv) e câmbio de quatro marchas da Volkswagen.  Apesar do sucesso comercial relativo do E400, a produção foi encerrada devido à limitada autonomia, tempo de recarga longo (cerca de 8 a 10 horas) e custo elevado das baterias.

This is the all-new Jaecoo 5! 

It’s fair to say the UK has had a bit of an influx of Chinese SUVs hitting our streets in 2025, but on looks alone, we think the Jaecoo 5 may be one of the best new entrants we've seen all year!

It’s available as either an ICE or EV, but is it just style over substance? Or should you settle for a more established brand for your next SUV? Let’s take a closer look…

Starting with the exterior design, the Jaecoo is giving us serious Range Rover vibes. We’ve got our hands on the range-topping edition, which means it's an EV without a grille at the front. It looks seriously sleek and smart, especially in this green paint job! Walk along the side, and you’d be forgiven for mistaking the Jaecoo 5 for a Range Rover Evoque! It’s a similar story around the back, with one feature once again borrowed from Range Rover - the rear windscreen wiper being hidden at the top of the rear window. 

Step inside, and the Jaecoo 5 has a very premium-feeling interior. There are soft-touch materials across the dash and high up on the doors, and sitting in the centre of the dash is a huge vertical screen. The infotainment system comes with loads of customisation, while also having the option to wirelessly connect to Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. There’s a small, customisable digital driver display, and the range-topping version we have here also comes with leatherette on the seats! 

The entry-level Jaecoo 5 is powered by a 1.6-litre turbo petrol that delivers 147hp. The range-topping edition we have here is an EV, which is equipped with a 61kWh battery that’s good for a range of up to 248 miles. It’s also equipped with a single electric motor, which produces 204hp. 

The Jaecoo 5 has a starting price of only £24,505, while the range-topping car we have here is only £30,505! So what do you think - is the Jaecoo 5 one of the best-value cars available today? You’ll need to stick with Mat to see for yourself!

title: 2026 BYD Atto 2 Small Electric SUV Review Australia: Price Specs Range
description:
Tom and Joy from the Ludicrous Feed YouTube channel review the BYD Atto 2 in Sydney, Australia, covering the two trims (Dynamic at $31,990 and Premium at $35,990 MSRP, plus ~$4,000 driveaway). The Atto 2 is a front-wheel drive small SUV with a 130 kW motor, 290 Nm torque, 0-100 km/h in 7.9 seconds, a 51.3 kWh BYD Blade LFP battery, and a WLTP range of 345 km. It supports 7 kW AC charging, 82 kW DC fast charging, and V2L. The review walks around the sensible, unassuming exterior, shows the 380L boot with 60/40 split folding seats, flat floor, and no power tailgate. Inside, the Premium trim adds a moon roof with powered sun shade, heated and ventilated front seats, wireless charging, a larger centre screen, 360-degree camera, auto-folding mirrors, and powered front seats. The infotainment runs wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto with physical shortcut buttons. On the road, the ride is described as firm but with some body roll due to height, regen braking is light (no one-pedal driving), and the car feels transition-friendly for drivers moving from petrol or diesel. Charging is tested at a Tesla Supercharger (works via CCS2). The review compares the Atto 2 to rivals like the MG4 EV Urban, GAC Aion UT, Jaecoo J5, Kia EV3, and Leapmotor B10, noting that while rivals may drive better or offer more value, the BYD wins on dealer and service centre availability across regional Australia, strong local support, and an unthreatening, practical ownership experience | Video by Tom Gan (Tesla Tom) and Joy of Ludicrous Feed from Sydney Australia April 2026

title: Range Rover (2026) - The City's Magnificent Ultra Luxury SUV!
description:
2026 Land Rover Range Rover
Price: $115,450–$247,850

Overview

You might primarily see Range Rovers at the mall or idling in front of the valet stands of posh restaurants, but Land Rover's legendary off-road capability means these stately-looking luxury SUVs can venture way off the grid, too. An air suspension provides plenty of ground clearance when needed, and the standard four-wheel-drive system has terrain modes tuned for multiple surfaces.

But even when you're meandering along with the lesser traffic, the Range Rover delights with a supremely plush cabin, a ride that glides over bumps, and a commanding view of the road. There's a wide range of available powertrains, including a plug-in hybrid option with some limited electric driving range. Off-road or on, a Range is a top-shelf pour.

Expert Tip: Due to its combination of off-road capability and high-end interior, the Range Rover has few rivals other than the Mercedes-Benz G-class. The Range Rover gets the edge over the Benz by offering more interior space and an available third row of seats. 

Engine, Transmission, and Performance

    Engines: 395-hp turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six, 523-hp twin-turbocharged 4.4-liter V-8, turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six and one electric motor (542-hp combined), 606-hp twin-turbo 4.4-liter V-8
    Transmission: 8-speed automatic
    Drivetrain: four-wheel drive

The Range Rover is available with a quartet of powertrains, starting with a turbocharged inline-six with a 48-volt hybrid system dubbed P400 that develops 395 horsepower. During our initial test drive, it proved to be silky smooth and provided adequate pep to tug the large Range Rover around. A 523-hp twin-turbo 4.4-liter V-8 engine—Land Rover calls it P530—is even swifter and cranks up the Range Rover's towing capacity to 8200 pounds.

A 542-hp plug-in-hybrid option—called P550e—is also available but only on the short-wheelbase models, and the range-topping SV comes with a 606-hp V-8 called P615. The Range Rover's ride is suitably plush, and with its adjustable air suspension set to Comfort mode, it floats down the road. Turning the dial to Dynamic mode firms things up some, but the big Rover still aims for a comfort-first mission. And of course, serious off-road chops are standard.
